newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher in quiet trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly higher in quiet trading on Tuesday and traders said the market was stabilising at the current level.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.28 percent, or 0.67 points, to 237.26 on all-share turnover of 121 million shekels against 132 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.21 percent higher at 246.03.

"The market made a very big move since the beginning of the year and now it is expected to stabilise at the current level. The rate cut was within expectations and it did not affect trading at all," said Yigal Mizrahi, chief analyst at Nesuah Trading and Investments.
On Monday after the close of trading the Bank of Israel said it was lowering its key lending rate for February by 0.5 percentage point to an annualised 14.2 percent.

"Trading was very quiet today and investors remained indifferent to the rate decision. The session opened with a rise of 0.7 percent but during the day the positive momentum weakened," said a trader at Bank Leumi.
"In the long run I believe that the trend will remain positive, but the market needs some time to digest the recent rise," Mizrahi added.
Koor Industries fell 1.75 percent to 31,546 agorot. On Tuesday Canada's Nortel completed its purchase of 20 percent of Koor's Telrad unit for $45 million.
Koor president's Benjamin Gaon said he now planned to take Telrad public as soon as possible.

The most active shares were Israel Chemicals, which rose 1.5 percent to 355 agorot on turnover of 7.0 million shekels; Bank Haopalim, which rose 2.25 percent to 602 agorot on volume of 5.9 million shekels; and Supersol, which lost 0.25 percent to 892 agorot on turnover of five million shekels.
